facts.text: A liquid staking token (LST) is a tokenized representation of staked tokens on a proof-of-stake chain that keeps earning staking rewards and stays usable in DeFi. Restaking lets staked tokens or LSTs secure extra protocols for extra rewards, and a liquid restaking token (LRT) makes that restaked position liquid. Lido's ReGOOSE post (May 2024) calls the LST 'a commoditized software offering' and says an LRT is 'closer to ETH-denominated mutual funds or tokenized deposits in an Ethereum lending market', so LRTs are less likely to gain deep liquidity and network effects.

An LST is a token for staked assets on a proof-of-stake chain that keeps earning staking rewards while staying usable in DeFi. An LRT is a token that makes a restaked position (staked tokens, LSTs, or native BTC tokens securing extra protocols) liquid. Lido's ReGOOSE post frames LRTs as the riskier, actively managed product and the LST as the commoditized one.

Chaos Labs' post-Pectra scenarios for Lido wstETH cover the consensus layer only, not AVS slashing. An isolated slashing costs about 0% of Lido stake (22.48 ETH). A majority consensus-client bug with a 13-day inactivity leak (about 30% of Lido operators on the faulty client) costs about 6.77% (634,648 ETH), with about $350M of Aave liquidations and $233K of bad debt. A minority-client bug with slashing costs about 15%, with $824M of liquidations and $48M of bad debt. Lido's slashing insurance fund held about 6,500 stETH at the time.

ChaosLabs modelled consensus-layer penalties for Lido wstETH after Pectra. Single-operator slashing or downtime costs about 0% of Lido stake (22.48 ETH for an ~8,192 ETH isolated slashing). A majority consensus-client bug with a 13-day inactivity leak costs about 6.77% (634,648 ETH), roughly $350M of Aave liquidations and about $233K of bad debt. A minority-client bug with slashing costs about 15%. The model covers LSTs only, not AVS slashing.

Chaos Labs modelled consensus-layer penalties for Lido's wstETH after Pectra, assuming 34M ETH staked and no operator above about 2.7% of Lido stake. Isolated operator slashing of about 8,192 ETH costs 22.48 ETH (about 0% of Lido stake). A majority consensus-client bug with a 13-day inactivity leak costs 634,647.9 ETH (6.77%), about $350M of Aave liquidations and $233K of bad debt. A minority-client bug with slashing costs 1,409,226.8 ETH (about 15%), $824M of liquidations and $48M of bad debt. The model covers LSTs only, not AVS slashing.

EigenLayer TVL has fallen roughly 70-75% from its 2025 level. The Block reported an all-time high of $20.1B in early June 2024. DefiLlama figures give $19.00B on 2025-10-04 (Sevim and Torres) and $22.06B in August 2025 (Blockhead), then $5.10B in late September 2026 (Blockhead) and $5.72B on 2026-11-06 (DefiLlama API). These are USD values, and ETH/USD fell 47% in H1 2026 (Lido), so part of the drop is price.

Pectra (Electra) changed Ethereum consensus-layer slashing. The consensus spec sets MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA at 2,048 ETH, MIN_ACTIVATION_BALANCE at 32 ETH and MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT_ELECTRA at 4,096. EIP-7251 describes the old initial penalty as 1/32 of effective balance, and LlamaRisk and Chaos Labs both report it fell to 1/4096.

When an issuer's own frontend is gone, third-party routes can still convert the LST. In the Lido case, a Sanctum team member told DL News that holders could trade stSOL for SOL or other LSTs through Sanctum, Cointelegraph noted users pointing to Sanctum or Jupiter, and a Marinade contributor told SolanaFloor the Marinade app can redelegate any stake account or LST instantly. SolanaFloor is a subsidiary of Jito Network, a Marinade competitor, and the Marinade statement is the contributor's own.

An LST tokenizes staked tokens on a proof-of-stake chain and keeps earning staking rewards while it stays usable in DeFi. An LRT tokenizes a restaked position, where staked tokens or LSTs also secure other protocols for extra rewards. The SoK paper says LRT architecture, token model and peg mechanism match those of LSTs. Kelp's rsETH shows the pattern: users deposit ETH, the protocol routes it through EigenLayer, and users get a tradeable receipt.

An LRT exit stacks several delays. The LRT adds its own buffer or cooldown on top of EigenLayer's 14-day withdrawal delay (ELIP-002; Kiln says it was 7 days before). In 2024 Renzo used hourly-replenished withdrawal buffers and a 3-day cooldown that LlamaRisk said would rise to 7 days once slashing launched. For native restaking, Gauntlet adds that exiting 5,000-10,000 validators on Ethereum takes about 6 days. Gauntlet says both secondary liquidity and redemption capacity are limited when liquidators sell LRT collateral.

An EigenLayer-forum thread (opened 2026-05-04) reports that on 2026-03-29 the 'EigenYields Yield AVS' used redistributable slashing to move delegated stETH into the operator EigenYields' own vaults. The operator says it announced the allocation on X on 2026-04-13 and that delegators get receipt tokens claimable from 2026-05-12, with redemptions every 24-48 hours. The thread title says '~250M' with no unit. A user's on-chain recomputation from SlashExecuted events in 10 self-slash transactions (2026-09-06) gives about $74M. Pectra activated on Ethereum mainnet on 2025-05-07 (epoch 364032), and EIP-7251 raised the maximum effective balance from 32 ETH to 2,048 ETH (ethereum.org). LlamaRisk says the initial slashing penalty fell from 1/32 to 1/4096 of effective balance. It also says one slashed consolidated validator can lose up to 64 times more than a 32 ETH validator, and that correlated slashing of a few large validators raises correlation penalties. Chaos Labs models the post-Pectra regime with 'dramatically reduced initial slashing penalties' and a rounding fix so every slashing carries a non-zero correlation

Before delegating to a public EigenLayer operator, or choosing operators for an LRT, check the operator's allocation delay, AVS membership and whether it is still active. ELIP-016 documents public operators with a 0-day allocation delay and others that stopped operating while still holding delegations, and ELIP-006 says a compromised operator can stand up its own AVS to steal stake. A user-built scanner discussed in the EigenYields thread flags operators with a 0-day allocation delay and tiny AVS membership.

At launch EigenLayer burned slashed funds: ERC-20 tokens went to a dead address and natively restaked ETH was locked in EigenPod contracts (ELIP-002, Kiln). On 2025-04-17 Eigen Labs listed 'slashing with redistribution' as coming soon. ELIP-006 (created 2025-04-30, status merged) then added redistributable operator sets.

EigenLayer's own specs treat an operator-created or hijacked AVS as a known theft path under redistributable slashing. ELIP-006 warns that 'If an Operator itself is compromised, it may stand-up its own AVS to steal user funds' and tells stakers to weigh operator reputation. ELIP-016 (status merged, created 2026-05-20) adds that an operator with a 0-day allocation delay can have delegated assets 'instantaneously allocated and redistributed out of EigenLayer', and that some public operators still holding delegations have stopped operating. It adds a 7-day (50,400-block) slash-resolution delay an

ELIP-002 sets the withdrawal delay and the deallocation delay at 100,800 blocks (about 14 days). A queued withdrawal stays slashable until the delay ends. A new deposit or delegation becomes slashable at once in proportion to allocated stake, with no activation delay. Kiln (2025-01-15) independently reports that the staker exit queue rose from 7 to 14 days. ELIP-002 also lists a 17.5-day allocation-configuration delay. Current mainnet values were not re-read because docs.eigencloud.xyz returned HTTP 403.

ELIP-002 lets an AVS slash any operator in its sets 'for any reason'. Slashing need not be objectively attributable on-chain, and the protocol provides no veto. The spec urges AVSs to add their own timelock, veto or fraud-proof windows because buggy slashing logic can ship. An LRT holder therefore depends on each AVS's slashing design, not only on EigenLayer's.

Blockhead, citing CoinDesk and DefiLlama category data, reports that the restaking category held $10.02B and earned $99,977 in fees in the prior week, while liquid staking held $51.87B and earned $27.35M, about 53 times more per dollar. It also reports that the five largest remaining LRTs (Renzo, Kelp, Swell, Puffer, Bedrock) earned $953,350 combined gross profit in Q2 2026, down from $2.18M three quarters earlier. These figures were not traced back to DefiLlama in this pass.
The Block calls the 2026 exploit Kelp's second rsETH security incident in about a year. In April 2025 a fee-contract bug caused excess minting of rsETH, and The Block says no user funds were lost.

Do not price LRT collateral from thin DEX pools. Gauntlet found the Morpho ezETH/WETH oracle drew on four pools (Balancer ezETH/WETH, Balancer ezETH/weETH/rswETH, Curve and Uniswap V3). Balancer's WETH liquidity fell from about 4,000 to as low as 500 WETH as holders and liquidators sold, which pushed the oracle down and triggered more liquidations. Gauntlet said an exchange-rate oracle would likely have caused fewer liquidations and noted its wstETH/WETH markets already use one. Curve suggested an EMA oracle with a suitable half-life. Capital moved from restaking to simple LSTs after the Kelp exploit. Lido's H1 2026 report (a self-interested source) says restaking contracted, EigenLayer's stETH deposits were undelegated, ether.fi shifted from restaking to liquid staking, the Simple LST segment rose to 22.6% of staked ETH by 2026-06-30, and the 'APR Maxis' segment fell from 17% to 6.5%. DefiLlama independently shows EigenCloud TVL falling from $9.92B (2026-04-17) to $4.38B (2026-06-30), which is 45% down to 30% of Lido's TVL.

In H1 2026 capital moved from restaking toward simple LSTs. Lido's H1 report says the Simple LST segment (stETH-led) rose to 22.6% of staked ETH by 2026-06-30 as EigenLayer's stETH deposits were undelegated and ether.fi shifted from restaking to liquid staking. It says the 'APR Maxis' segment fell from 17% to 6.5% after the Kelp incident. Blockhead adds that less than 1% of ether.fi's assets were restaked in August 2026. Lido competes with LRTs, so read its framing as a vendor view.

The FTX collapse (9 Nov 2022) produced a large Solana unstake run. CoinDesk reported a record deactivation of 54 million SOL, over 15% of staked SOL, due within hours. Lido's stSOL traded 7% below SOL that day while Marinade's mSOL traded above SOL. Marinade's own account says mSOL traded at a discount in Epoch 370 for lack of liquidity and that its liquid-unstake pool ran dry. Marinade's forum proposal says the pool was depleted within hours and stayed at zero for about three and a half days; a forum reply dates the depletion from 9 Nov 8am to 12 Nov about 5pm.

On 2026-04-18 (17:35 UTC) an attacker drained 116,500 rsETH (about $292M, roughly 18% of supply) from Kelp DAO's LayerZero OFT bridge. Galaxy reports Kelp had configured a 1-of-1 verifier. This was a bridge exploit, not an AVS slashing event. Galaxy says mainnet rsETH stays backed by Kelp's underlying staking deposits and that stETH and wstETH were unaffected. Kelp paused its contracts about 46 minutes after the drain.

LRT growth in 2024 was incentive-driven. Lido's ReGOOSE (2024-05-10) says LRTs drew stake with 'billions of dollars in speculation-driven, unsustainable subsidies', that 5M ETH ($15B) sat in EigenLayer mostly before any AVS was live, and that stETH share fell from 32% to 29%. The Block (2024-07-18) reports EigenLayer TVL fell about 27%, from $20.1B to $14.66B, and Renzo's from $4.07B to $2.09B, after the EIGEN and REZ launches ended airdrop campaigns. Gauntlet (2024-12-20) says LRT-driven lending had 'honed in on maximizing restaking airdrop and point potential'.

JIP-6 (2024-09-24) split the rollout into Deposits (Vault Program, 10 bps withdrawal fee), Staking (Restaking Program plus a Jito Rewards NCN taking 4% of NCN rewards) and Slashing. In the thread Jito said third-party teams (Renzo, Fragmetric, Kyros) would run VRT migrations and user support, and that any SPL token can become a VRT if NCN developers, VRT providers and node operators all agree. The current JitoSOL guide still lists a 4% protocol reward fee and a 0.1% protocol withdrawal fee.

On 2026-08-06 ether.fi announced that it had removed all restaking exposure from weETH, which is now a plain liquid staking token. Restaking moved to a separate Symbiotic-based token, weETHs. Blockhead, quoting ether.fi documentation, says less than 1% of ether.fi's assets remained restaked as of August and EigenPod withdrawal credentials are due to be removed by Q4 2026. The CEO told CoinDesk 'There were no meaningful yield opportunities in restaking' (as quoted by Blockhead). DefiLlama's ether.fi Stake TVL fell from $12.43B (2025-08-14) to $4.24B (2026-11-06).

In H1 2026 capital moved out of restaking into simple LSTs. Lido's report says EigenLayer restaking contracted, EigenLayer's stETH deposits were undelegated, ether.fi shifted from restaking to liquid staking, and the Simple LST category (stETH-led) rose to 22.6%. The Defiant reports ether.fi removed restaking from weETH and moved it into a separate Symbiotic-based token, weETHs.

Blockhead, citing DefiLlama data, reports that restaking pays little next to liquid staking. Restaking held $10.02B on 2026-09-08 and earned $99,977 in fees in the prior week. Liquid staking held $51.87B and earned $27.35M, about 53 times more per dollar. Renzo, Kelp, Swell, Puffer and Bedrock together made $953,350 gross profit in Q2 2026, down from $2.18M three quarters earlier. ether.fi's gross profit fell 47%, from $18.71M in Q3 2025 to $9.99M in Q2 2026.

Restaking TVL in 2024 was incentive-driven. Lido's ReGOOSE post (2024-05-10) says users had deposited 5M ETH (about $15B) in EigenLayer, mostly before any AVS was live, drawn by 'unsustainable' LRT subsidies, while stETH's share fell from 32% to 29%. The Block (2024-07-18) reports EigenLayer TVL fell about 27% from a $20.1B peak to $14.66B and Renzo's fell from $4.07B to $2.09B once EIGEN and REZ launches ended airdrop campaigns. DefiLlama's Renzo series shows a $4.05B peak on 2024-05-28 and $0.10B on 2026-11-06.

Protocol responses split by asset type. SparkLend, Fluid, Upshift, Yearn, Beefy and Pendle froze or paused rsETH markets. Morpho reported only about $1M of exposure in two isolated markets. Lido paused deposits to its earnETH product (about $21.6M of rsETH, roughly 9% of the vault, per Rekt) while saying stETH and wstETH were unaffected. Ethena, ether.fi, Curve and Lombard paused LayerZero bridges or routes despite having no rsETH exposure.

LRT and restaking TVL proved incentive-driven in 2024. EigenLayer TVL fell about 27% (from a $20.1B early-June peak to $14.66B) by 2024-07-18, and Renzo TVL nearly halved ($4.07B to $2.09B). The Block attributes this mainly to token launches and airdrop endings (EIGEN, REZ). Lido's ReGOOSE post separately called LRT yield dependent on subsidies and points.

Sevim and Torres (daily data 2024-01-22 to 2025-04-17, 452 observations) find Renzo's revenue tracks EigenLayer TVL almost one-for-one (coefficient 0.98), plus ezETH yield and Renzo's L2 TVL. Renzo's own Ethereum TVL is not significant, and model R-squared is 0.28-0.44. As of 2025-10-09 about 90,862 ezETH (29.8% of Renzo's total) sat on other chains, mostly Linea. A 3.33% depeg would make every maximum-LTV ezETH position on Aave v3 Linea (64,890 ezETH) liquidatable. The authors call their results exploratory and limited to one protocol and one market phase.

Third-party teams, not Jito, run the VRT products. JIP-6 (2024-11-14) says Renzo, Fragmetric and Kyros handle VRT migrations and each is responsible for its own frontend and user support. The withdrawal guide's examples use a BNSOL vault (bzSOL) and ezSOL. DefiLlama still shows KYROS and BNSOL balances in Jito Restaking on 2026-11-06, each under 1% of TVL.

On 9 Nov 2022, after FTX collapsed, Lido's stSOL traded about 7% below SOL while mSOL traded above SOL; LSTs normally trade at a slight premium. SOL was down nearly 60% in a week and over 15% of staked SOL was set to deactivate.

The Kelp loss reached lenders through Aave. The attacker deposited 89,567 rsETH on Aave (Ethereum and Arbitrum) and borrowed 82,650 WETH and 821 wstETH (Rekt, Decrypt). Rekt reports WETH pool utilization hit 100%, and Galaxy reports primary stablecoin markets at 100%. Aave had allowed rsETH as WETH E-Mode collateral in January 2026 at up to 93% LTV, up from 72% (SparkLend 72%, Fluid about 75%). Galaxy puts the Aave TVL drop at $26.4B to $17.9B in about two days.

A volunteer's Flipside query, shared in the Marinade forum on 29 Nov 2022, put the worst mSOL sell price at about a 10% discount to SOL during 9-12 Nov 2022. It showed some stSOL sells at far larger discounts (the author cut outliers below 0.5 from the chart). Forum readers said the deepest prints were bought back quickly. The author said they coded the queries in a hurry and asked for review. No reviewed price series was posted.

Lido's H1 2026 report: total staked ETH rose 19% (36.3M to 43.1M ETH, including the entry queue) and Lido captured 5.7% of the increase. Institutional staking rose from 25.9% to 35.3% of staked ETH. The treasury firm Bitmine gained 10.06 points to 11.5%. ether.fi held 4.1% (down 1.79 points). The USD value of the staking market fell from about $108B to $68B as ETH/USD fell 47%.

Most new ETH stake is not entering LSTs or LRTs. Lido's H1 2026 report says total staked ETH grew 19% (36.3M to 43.1M ETH) and Lido captured 5.7% of the increase, so its share fell from 23.93% to 21.18% by 2026-06-30. Institutional staking rose from 25.9% to 35.3% of staked ETH. Top entities on 2026-06-30: Lido 21.2%, Bitmine 11.5%, Coinbase 10.9%, Binance 7.9%, ether.fi 4.1%. Four Pillars (published 2026-06-02) gives 20.7% for Lido, down from 32.5% in May 2022, and credits ETFs, ETPs and direct institutional staking.

A December 2024 Gauntlet simulation on the EigenLayer forum (a model, not an observed event) finds that lenders price LRTs at NAV, so a slash cuts collateral value directly. With over $1.5B of weETH supplied above 92% LTV on Aave (liquidation threshold 95%), a roughly 2% weETH slash could force about $500M of immediate liquidations and about $1B of EigenLayer TVL decay (about 7 times the slash), taking nearly 150 hours to clear. Lido's share of all staked ETH was 21.18% on 2026-06-30, down from 23.93% at the start of 2026 (including the entry queue), while Lido TVL rose to 9.13M ETH. Lido attributes the fall to new capital entering exchange and digital-asset-treasury segments. Four Pillars independently puts the share at 20.7% in June 2026, down from 32.5% in May 2022.

Lido's share of all staked ETH fell to 21.18% on 2026-06-30 from 23.93% at the start of 2026 (Lido, including the entry queue), while Lido TVL rose from 8.74M to 9.13M ETH. Four Pillars (2026-06-02) puts the share at 20.7%, down from 32.5% in May 2022, and says Lido's stake rose from about 4.1M to 8.6M ETH. Both attribute the fall to faster growth elsewhere (exchanges, institutions, treasuries such as Bitmine). Neither blames LRT competition for the 2026 decline.

Both LRT incidents hurt lenders through collateral parameters and oracles. In 2026 Aave's E-Mode allowed rsETH at up to 93% LTV (SparkLend 72%), Aave froze rsETH markets, and Aave TVL fell from about $26.4B to $17.9B in two days. In 2024 Gauntlet moved WETH to lower-LLTV markets and evaluated exchange-rate oracles that it believed would have caused fewer liquidations. A DeFi integrator who treats an LRT like an LST gets exposed to risks the LST does not carry.

USD TVL changes mix flows with ETH price, so compare LST and LRT momentum with ratios or ETH-denominated figures. Lido's H1 2026 report says ETH/USD fell 47% in H1 2026 while Lido staking TVL rose from 8.74M to 9.13M ETH (including the entry queue). DefiLlama's USD series for Lido fell from $26.09B (2025-12-31) to $14.50B (2026-06-30), then recovered to $24.08B by 2026-09-08 as ETH rebounded (ETH was $1,569 on 2026-06-30 and $2,441 on 2026-08-25).

DefiLlama's series (pulled 2026-11-06) shows EigenLayer, now listed as EigenCloud, at $5.72B TVL against a record $22.06B on 2025-08-14, and Lido at $21.77B against a record of about $42.5B on 2025-08-23. EigenCloud's TVL as a share of Lido's TVL (computed from the two series) fell from 53% on 2025-08-14 to 45% on 2026-04-17, 30% on 2026-06-30 and 26% on 2026-11-06. Blockhead (2026-09-29) cites the same $22.06B peak.

LlamaRisk modelled two loss paths (relayed by Galaxy and Rekt). If Kelp spreads the loss over all rsETH (a 15.12% haircut), Aave bad debt is about $123.7M, with $91.8M on Ethereum Core. If the loss falls only on L2 rsETH (a 73.54% haircut), bad debt is about $230.1M, all on L2s. On 2026-05-12 The Block put the bad debt at about $190M.

The attacker immediately posted the stolen rsETH as collateral. Rekt counts 89,567 rsETH supplied on Aave V3 (eMode 3, about 99% effective LTV) against 82,650 WETH and 821 wstETH borrowed, plus smaller borrows on Compound V3 (about $39.4M) and Euler (about $0.84M). Aave froze rsETH and WETH markets and WETH pools hit 100% utilization. Galaxy says 112,204 rsETH (about 15% of post-exploit supply) became unbacked at the adapter. LlamaRisk's 2026-04-20 scenarios put Aave bad debt at $123.7M (loss spread over all rsETH) or $230.1M (loss isolated to L2 rsETH); The Block (2026-05-12) says about $190M

On 2024-04-24 the ezETH/WETH oracle on Morpho first dipped below 1.0 at 02:25 UTC, and the first liquidation came at 02:29:47 UTC. 145 of 146 liquidations (138 in the 0.86 LLTV market, 8 in the 0.77 market) were done by 02:52:35 UTC. The 0.86 market took 10.96 WETH of insolvency, of which 7.12 WETH (11 bps of supply) hit Gauntlet's LRT Core vault. DL News reports ezETH fell as low as $700 on some markets (79% in under an hour) and that 250+ users lost about $56M to liquidations across protocols.

Gauntlet measured a beta of roughly 0.2 between ETH price moves and LRT dislocation from NAV, excluding weETH: a 10% ETH drop could open a 2% dislocation. weETH held up better in downturns because its immediate-withdrawal capacity absorbed LRT-to-ETH conversions that other LRTs routed through DEXs.

The 2024-04-24 ezETH depeg was a liquidity and redemption failure, not a slashing event. After Renzo's REZ tokenomics announcement ezETH traded as low as $700 on some markets, down 79% in under an hour, while Renzo allowed no withdrawals, so selling was the only exit (DL News). DL News counts about $56M of liquidations (Gearbox 115 users, Morpho 146 users). Gauntlet records the ezETH/WETH oracle first dipping below 1.0 at 02:25 UTC and 145 of 146 Morpho liquidations done by 02:52:35 UTC. Curve says its shallow ezETH pool ($3.2M TVL, $36M volume) saw a 20% depeg, and contrasts that with 'sudden

Multi-chain expansion is a double-edged sword for an LRT. Sevim and Torres (arXiv 2604.03274) find Renzo revenue is driven by EigenLayer value locked, LRT yield and multi-chain spread, and that bridging adds risk on top of restaking risk. At Renzo's current size they find no systemic risk. Kelp's rsETH bridge loss in April 2026 shows the bridge layer can fail without any slashing.

The Kelp drain hit the bridged L2 float, not mainnet backing. Galaxy (citing LlamaRisk, Aave's risk manager) and Rekt (citing Aave) both state that mainnet rsETH remains backed by Kelp's underlying ETH staking deposits. After the exploit 112,204 rsETH (about 15% of post-exploit supply) was unbacked at the bridge adapter. The adapter held 40,373 rsETH against 152,577 rsETH outstanding on L2s, a maximum 26.46% pro-rata L2 backing from the adapter alone. Galaxy says Lido's stETH and wstETH were unaffected.

Depeg risk follows the redemption path for LSTs and LRTs alike. The SoK paper reports temporary LST depegs in extreme events (Terra/Luna, FTX). rETH traded below peg then because ETH could not be unstaked before Shanghai, so arbitrage could not close the gap. Gauntlet puts the recovery of stETH's Spring 2022 depeg at a few hours for a few percent. ezETH's 2024 depeg happened while Renzo had not enabled withdrawals (LlamaRisk).

On 2026-04-18 (17:35 UTC) an attacker delivered a forged LayerZero message that made Kelp DAO's rsETH OFT adapter release 116,500 rsETH on Ethereum (about $290-292M, about 18% of circulating supply by Rekt's count). Kelp's route used a 1-of-1 verifier (LayerZero Labs' DVN). The attackers poisoned the RPC nodes that verifier read, so it signed a packet for a burn that never happened. LayerZero preliminarily attributes the attack to North Korea's Lazarus Group. It was a bridge-verification failure, not AVS slashing or a loss in the staking base. A delegator reported on the EigenLayer forum (2026-05-04) that EigenYields' own Yield AVS used redistributable slashing on 2026-03-29 to move delegated stETH into the operator's vaults. The delegator's queued withdrawal of about 1.52 stETH (about $3,570) returned 1 wei. The operator replied that it was a planned allocation announced on X on 2026-04-13, and promised receipt tokens for 2026-05-12; the delegator claimed them on 2026-05-13 and queued an unstake. Li Li's arXiv paper (v2, 2024-12-16) frames EigenLayer and Lido as complementary fixes for proof-of-stake problems: high validator entry barriers, illiquid staked ETH and staking-pool centralization. The abstract mentions no LRT incidents and no AVS slashing risk. Only the abstract was read, so treat this as an optimistic framing that predates mainnet slashing.

An LRT holder carries every LST risk plus extra layers. LlamaRisk calls this 'dual slashing risk': consensus-layer penalties on the underlying ETH, plus AVS slashing under EigenLayer from 2025-04-17. The SoK paper says restaking 'multiplies the slashing risks as the stake is locked in multiple services'. Lido's ReGOOSE post calls the 'more risky and actively-managed nature of LRTs' a poor fit for institutions.

The 2024-04-24 ezETH depeg was a liquidity and redemption failure, not a slashing event: AVS slashing did not exist until 2025-04-17. Renzo's REZ tokenomics gave ezETH holders 5% of supply against 2.5% for Binance launchpool users, and holders sold. Renzo had not enabled withdrawals, so selling on DEXs was the only exit (DL News). LlamaRisk says the price fell up to 78% on some venues when 'withdrawals were not enabled at the time', and that withdrawals activated in mid-June 2024. Gauntlet calls the event a liquidity crunch.

Lido on Solana shows the failure mode where the exit path itself breaks. Lido announced the sunset on 16 Oct 2023 (no new stake) and ended frontend support on 5 Feb 2024, leaving only the CLI. In March 2024 a flaw in the withdrawal logic also blocked CLI withdrawals. DL News (2 Apr 2024) counted about $24 million, over 112,000 stSOL and more than 31,000 wallets still held; Cointelegraph counted 31,588 holders. Treating an LRT like an LST in lending parameters is the main collateral anti-pattern. Gauntlet (2024-12) found over $1.5B of weETH supplied on Aave at above 92% LTV (well over $1.3B of debt) against a 95% liquidation threshold. Its simulation, not an observed event, showed a 2% weETH slash cutting EigenLayer TVL by about $1B (almost 7 times the slash) and taking about 150 hours to clear liquidations. In 2026 Aave let rsETH borrow WETH at up to 93% in E-Mode. Galaxy expects LRT and LST collateral parameters to tighten and looping to migrate back to wstETH and weETH.

EigenLayer slashing is opt-in. AVSs group operators into Operator Sets with their own slashing conditions, and an operator must opt into each set. Operators allocate part of their delegated stake as Unique Stake that only one AVS can slash, which isolates cross-AVS risk. A staker is exposed only if their operator joins a slashable set.

Failure mode for the arbitrage: if unstaking itself is blocked, no arbitrage closes the gap. After Lido sunset its Solana protocol (frontend removed Feb 2024), a smart-contract flaw blocked withdrawals; DL News (2 Apr 2024) reported over $24M, more than 112,000 stSOL, across more than 31,000 wallets still held. Sanctum was named as an exit route for stSOL-to-SOL swaps.

Lido's 2024 ReGOOSE proposal by Hasu argued stETH should always stay an LST, become the leading collateral in restaking markets, and support Ethereum-aligned validator services (starting with preconfirmations) without adding risk for stETH holders. It did not rule out a future stETH-based LRT. The Snapshot vote ran 2024-05-16 to 2024-05-23, and its outcome was not read here.

Lido's ReGOOSE proposal (Hasu, 2024-05-10) argued that stETH should always stay an LST, become the top collateral in restaking markets so stakers can opt into more risk, and support validator services such as preconfirmations without extra risk to stETH holders (for example through a dedicated cover fund). It did not rule out a separate Lido LRT product. The Snapshot vote ended 2024-05-23 and its result was not found in the thread text.

On 2026-04-18 at 17:35 UTC an attacker released 116,500 rsETH (about $292M, roughly 18% of circulating supply) from Kelp's mainnet LayerZero OFT escrow. The attacker used a forged cross-chain packet that claimed to come from Unichain. Kelp ran a 1-of-1 verifier, with LayerZero Labs as the sole DVN. LayerZero's post-mortem calls the method RPC poisoning, not key theft, and preliminarily attributes it to Lazarus Group's TraderTraitor unit. Kelp paused its contracts 46 minutes after the drain. This was a bridge-verification failure, not AVS slashing and not an Ethereum consensus event.

An LRT holder stacks risk layers that a plain LST holder does not. Both face Ethereum consensus-layer penalties, which reach holders through oracle-reported rebases. An LRT adds AVS slashing if the operator opts in, plus LRT-protocol smart-contract risk. Lido's ReGOOSE post says restaking adds extra slashing conditions and that EigenLayer and LRT yields depended on subsidies and points programs it called unsustainable.

Review the whole bridge and custody stack, not only the token. Galaxy says a single verifier on Kelp's LayerZero setup had 'effective admin-level power over Aave's WETH markets', so risk review must cover every trust assumption in an asset's bridge and custody stack, and it expects tighter LTVs and more isolation-mode listings for LRTs. Rekt says every audit came back clean and the failed verification layer 'wasn't in any audit scope'. Sevim and Torres (arXiv 2604.03274) likewise call an LRT's multi-chain expansion 'a double-edged sword' because bridging adds bridge risk to restaking risk.

Gauntlet lists the properties that decide how a slash propagates through an LRT: the withdrawal queue, rewards structure, NAV oracle or exchange-rate module, secondary-market liquidity relative to volume, and insurance mechanisms. It proposes a lending killswitch that freezes new borrows during unexplained dislocations, and phased or redistributed slashing. Galaxy adds that risk review must cover every trust assumption in the asset's bridge and custody stack, not only the collateral asset.

Lending venues exposed lenders to LRT risk very differently. Galaxy reports Aave allowed rsETH as E-Mode collateral for WETH at 93% LTV (up from 72%) in January 2026, against 72% at SparkLend and about 75% at Fluid, and that Morpho's isolated markets held only about $1M of rsETH exposure. In the 2024 ezETH event Gauntlet's Morpho vault saw insolvency only in the 0.86-LLTV ezETH market (10.96 WETH); the 0.77-LLTV market had 8 liquidations and no insolvency.

A consensus-layer penalty reaches an LST holder through the protocol's accounting. Lido's bunker mode pauses withdrawal requests during a prolonged negative rebase so that exiting holders cannot dodge the loss (Chaos Labs). An AVS slash cuts delegator shares at once, including shares in queued withdrawals (ELIP-002), and Gauntlet models it as an immediate loss of an LRT's underlying funds.

On 2026-08-06 ether.fi announced that it had removed all restaking exposure from weETH, making weETH a pure LST. Restaking moved to weETHs, a separate LRT built on Symbiotic. Blockhead reports the last structural EigenLayer tie, the EigenPod withdrawal credentials, is due to go by Q4 2026. It quotes CEO Mike Silagadze: 'There were no meaningful yield opportunities in restaking', and adds 'perceived risk from stakers'.

Putting one LRT on 20+ chains behind a 1-of-1 bridge verifier made the bridge the weakest layer. Galaxy says one verifier had 'effective admin-level power over Aave's WETH markets'. Rekt relays a CoinDesk figure that about 40% of LayerZero apps ran 1-of-1, an on-chain scan finding 1,111 of about 3,500 OApps on strict 1-of-1, and a February 2025 BGD Labs warning in Aave governance that went unheeded. LayerZero said it will stop signing for 1-of-1 setups. Sevim and Torres reach the same point: bridging adds bridge risk to restaking risk.

At launch EigenLayer burned slashed funds (ERC-20 strategies sent to a dead address, native ETH locked in EigenPods). ELIP-006 added Redistributable Operator Sets: the AVS sets a redistributionRecipient when it creates the set, the address cannot be changed later and can be any address, and these sets cannot use the EIGEN or native-ETH strategies. So a staker's LST-strategy shares in such a set can be moved to an address the AVS chose.

Blame for the Kelp exploit is disputed. LayerZero's post-mortem says Kelp relied on LayerZero Labs as sole verifier, against its recommended multi-DVN model, and LayerZero says Kelp 'deployed multiDVN and then manually downgraded to a 1/1'. Kelp's 2026-05-06 memo says LayerZero staff directly approved the 1-of-1 setup across eight meetings over about 2.5 years and, citing Dune data, that about 47% of roughly 2,665 active LayerZero OApps used 1-of-1 (about $4.5B at risk). Researcher Banteg could not prove which configuration Kelp first deployed. Rekt notes LayerZero has not explained how attack

Under ELIP-006 a redistributing operator set fixes its redistributionRecipient at creation, and the address cannot change. Only ERC-20 strategies qualify, so EIGEN and native ETH are excluded; LSTs such as stETH are ERC-20s, though the spec does not name them. Operators opt in and carry a 'Redistributable' label. The spec describes no separate staker opt-in. It warns: 'If an Operator itself is compromised, it may stand-up its own AVS to steal user funds'. It names no redistribution-specific allocation delay or veto.

An LST holder bears Ethereum consensus-layer penalties. An LRT holder bears those plus AVS slashing for any slashable Operator Set the LRT's operators have joined, plus the LRT protocol's own contract, oracle and operator-selection risk. LlamaRisk calls this 'dual slashing exposure' for LRTs from the 2025-04-17 AVS slashing launch.

Pectra makes isolated slashing cheaper but shifts risk to correlated events. Chaos Labs models an isolated slashing on about 8,192 ETH of Lido stake at 22.48 ETH after Pectra versus 270.55 ETH before (down 91.7%). LlamaRisk warns that a consolidated 2,048 ETH validator can lose up to 64 times what a 32 ETH validator loses, and that correlation penalties could become much more severe when a few large validators are slashed together.

Sevim and Torres report that on 2025-10-09 about $19.23B was restaked, roughly 13% of the 35.7M ETH staked, of which $13.97B was native restaking and $4.06B liquid restaking. ether.fi's eETH held 65.4% of all LRTs, so the LRT market was concentrated in one issuer. The DefiLlama category table in the same paper lists ether.fi at $11.21B, so category definitions differ from the paper's own count.

Community monitoring exists for the redistributable-slashing risk. A user in the EigenYields thread published a Dune dashboard and a scanner repository (2026-09-06) that compute slashed totals directly from SlashExecuted events instead of trusting operator claims, and flag operators with a 0-day allocation delay and tiny AVS membership. The repository link given in the thread returned HTTP 404 when fetched, so the scanner itself was not inspected.

The Kelp exploit hit bridge-wrapped rsETH, not the staking base or plain LSTs. Galaxy says mainnet rsETH stays backed by Kelp's underlying ETH staking deposits and that stETH and wstETH were unaffected. DefiLlama's Kelp TVL barely moved ($1.59B on 2026-04-17, $1.64B on 04-18, $1.52B on 04-20). Lido's report says its EarnETH vault, which had rsETH exposure, fell from 110,600 ETH to 44,500 ETH with no user funds lost: first-loss cover paid 143.98 ETH, and the DAO committed up to 2,500 stETH to the rsETH relief effort.

Kelp's liquid-restaking TVL was $842.9M, against $1.44B on 2026-04-17, $1.52B on 2026-04-20 and $1.32B on 2026-05-31. All are USD values and move with the ETH price. All four endpoints come from one publisher.

EigenLayer timing parameters set how long a staker stays exposed. ELIP-002 sets WITHDRAWAL_DELAY and DEALLOCATION_DELAY at 100,800 blocks (about 14 days) and ALLOCATION_CONFIGURATION_DELAY at 126,000 blocks (about 17.5 days). A queued withdrawal stays slashable for the full 14 days. The operator's own ALLOCATION_DELAY has no protocol constraint, and new deposits and delegations are slashable at once in the allocated proportion. ELIP-016 (created 2026-05-20) repeats the 14-day escrow and 17.5-day initial period and says some public operators have since set their allocation delay to 0 days.
